label: Teltonika TSW101
description: Five-port gigabit automotive switch: 5x 1 GbE, PoE+ on four of them. The fifth port is the uplink; the other four power in-vehicle cameras, access points and routers from a 12 V or 24 V vehicle supply.
notes: Vendor figures (TSW101 datasheet v1.30, https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/4785183.pdf, and the TSW101 flyer 2023 v1.1): "Ethernet ETH 5 x ETH ports, 10/100/1000 Mbps, supports auto MDI/MDIX crossover"; "POE OUT PoE+ ports Port 1 - 4"; "PoE standards IEEE 802.3af (PoE, Type 1) and IEEE 802.3at (PoE+, Type 2), Alternative A"; "PoE Max Power per Port (at PSE) 30 W"; "Total PoE Power Budget (at PSE) 60 W". The flyer gives the panel split in words - "5 x 10/100/1000 Ethernet ports: 4 x PoE, 1 x Uplink" - and the datasheet names the powered sockets "Port 1 - 4", so eth5 is the uplink: declared `"poeOut": false` rather than left undeclared, because a copper port on a `poe-pse` device with no `poeOut` key is inferred to be a 15.4 W 802.3af source (the row previously had all five sourcing power). The four PSE ports carry the vendor's 30 W per-port ceiling instead of the `true` this row used to hold, the same shape as its TSW100/TSW200 siblings. The 60 W total is supply-dependent - the v1.5 datasheet footnotes 30 W maximum at 12 VDC against 60 W at 24 VDC - and the single budget field carries the ceiling; see the `poe` note. Automotive body: 2-pin power socket, 9-30 VDC, no separate PSU.

poe.note: Datasheet (TSW101, v1.30, 2026-06-01), POE OUT block, verbatim: "PoE+ ports Port 1 - 4"; "PoE standards IEEE 802.3af (PoE, Type 1) and IEEE 802.3at (PoE+, Type 2), Alternative A"; "PoE Max Power per Port (at PSE) 30 W"; "Total PoE Power Budget (at PSE) 60 W"; "Power consumption Idle: 0.64 W / Max: 2.31 W / PoE Max: 62.3 W"; and the cover: "4 x PoE+ ports ... 5 x Gigabit Ethernet ports". The flyer states the split in the panel's own words - "5 x 10/100/1000 Ethernet ports: 4 x PoE, 1 x Uplink" (TSW101_Flyer_2023_v1.1) - which is why port 5 carries no `poeOut`. The budget is supply-dependent and the single field cannot hold both: the older v1.5 datasheet footnotes "* Depends on connected power source. (30 W (max.) @ 12 VDC for total PD consumption; ... 60 W (max.) @ 24 VDC for total PD consumption)"; the 60 W row is the 24 V figure and therefore the ceiling, and a 12 V vehicle system funds 30 W. Read 2026-11-20.
